summary: Heath Cummings' Week 16 fantasy football wide receiver preview from CBSSports.com argues Chiefs rookie Rashee Rice is a must-start in the semifinals despite a tough-looking Raiders matchup. It covers key numbers (Rice's yards after catch, Deebo Samuel, Puka Nacua, Tyreek Hill), matchup tables for several receivers, waiver targets (Curtis Samuel, Demario Douglas, Dontayvion Wicks), and DFS picks (CeeDee Lamb as top play, Jaylen Waddle as contrarian).
one_line: Week 16 fantasy football WR preview: start Rashee Rice, add Curtis Samuel and Dontayvion Wicks, and target CeeDee Lamb or Jaylen Waddle in DFS.
key_facts: Rashee Rice has four straight games with at least nine targets and at least 14 PPR Fantasy points in each; he is WR29 on the season but is now borderline top-12.
Since Week 12, only Deebo Samuel and CeeDee Lamb have scored more PPR Fantasy points than Rashee Rice.
Rice scored 24.7 PPR Fantasy points against the Raiders in Week 12; the Raiders have allowed the 11th-fewest passing yards but the fourth-most yards after the catch.
69.9% of Rashee Rice's receiving yards have come after the catch, tops among wide receivers with at least 50 targets; his ADOT is 4.3.

Deebo Samuel (11.4 yards per target) is on pace to be the fourth player since 1992 to average more than 11 yards per target with at least 60 targets in multiple seasons, joining Tyreek Hill, Tyler Lockett and DeSean Jackson.
Puka Nacua needs 18 more catches to set the rookie record for most catches in a season.
Tyreek Hill missed last week's game and needs to average about 152.67 yards per game in his final three to reach his stated goal of 2,000 receiving yards.
Drake London averages 15.88 PPR FPPG at home this season and just 7.37 on the road.
Noah Brown has three games with at least 24.2 PPR points but zero points in two of his last three; he is called 'the Gabe Davis of the South'.
Curtis Samuel (WAS) was last week's top WR waiver add yet is only 57-58% rostered; he has three straight games of double-digit points and topped 19 in two of them.

Dontayvion Wicks (15% rostered) had a career-high seven targets in Week 15, and his snap share has risen three weeks in a row; he could be the best option if Christian Watson and Jayden Reed stay out.
Heath prefers CeeDee Lamb ($900 cheaper than Hill, who may not be 100%) as the top DFS play; Lamb has 103 catches, 1306 yards and 10 TDs.
Jaylen Waddle is the contrarian DFS play, with three of seven games over 19 PPR points and two over 26.
